summary: Porcupine Hills tower: a 1977 jet crash on its ridge killed the pilot and started fires; the register dates the present steel tower to 2003.

access.note: Register lists the tower as active with drive access. The observer lives at the lookout, and a 2018 visitor went in with the observer's permission. No source describes public visits.

events.note: Steel tower replaced the earliest, wooden tower, according to a 2018 hiking blog that draws on a guidebook (guidebook not read).
F-106A jet crashed into the ridge during a mock-attack exercise; fires broke out in the wreckage. The 37 m (120 ft) tower narrowly missed.
George Hames and his wife, who had duties at the lookout, were in the station trailer near the tower when the crash woke them.
Register construction year for the present steel tower.
Observer lives at the lookout; the 2018 season opened almost a month late because of snow.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1977 account gives 37 m (120 ft) for the tower then on the ridge; the register gives 30 m (98 ft) for the present tower. The sources do not explain the difference.
The 1970 steel tower (blog) and the 2003 construction year (register) are not in conflict: the register dates only the present tower, which the blog calls a replacement.

notes_for_editor: History rests on one 2018 Crowsnest Pass Herald column (the 1977 crash, the pilot's death, the 120 ft tower, the memorial), one 2018 hiking blog (the wooden first tower named Skyline Lookout, the 1970 steel tower; the blog cites Mike Potter's guidebook, which was not read), the register and the Alberta.ca page. The column spells the pilot's name three ways (Dennings, Denning, Henning); the story does not name him. The brief's access 'closed' and its note ('staffed March-October', 'please don't visit uninvited') appear in no source read; Alberta.ca says generally April to October, and access is recorded as restricted. The brief's agency 'Alberta Wildfire' is recorded as Alberta Agriculture and Forestry (Wildfire), which Alberta.ca names. The 2018 observer is not named. The memorial is at the crash site, which the column places on the south end of a ranch; the lookout is not stated to be on that ranch.
